Read out of saint.gr's line for 16 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Σαβίνος ο Αιγύπτιος», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Αβίβος από την Ερμούπολη», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 16 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученик Савин.“, with the rank words Свети мученик left off. The heading gives no city and no by-name — Hermopolis and his being an Egyptian are both in the body — so the bare forename is what the source gives.

death.note: doxologia.ro's life for the day: «Pe vremea împărăției lui Dioclețian (284-305), pentru prigonirea cea cumplită ce era asupra creștinilor». The reign is the interval the page prints; it gives no year of death.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 16 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Sabin Egipteanul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 16ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Σαβίνος ο Αιγύπτιος»

attestations.note: The page heads him «(; - 287)» and closes «έλαβε το στέφανο του μαρτυρίου το 287 μ.Χ.», while it opens the account with the persecution of Diocletian «(284 - 305 μ.Χ.)»; the corpus's interval is that reign, from doxologia, and is left as it stands, with the page's year recorded here. It names the eparch Arrianos, has the Christians of the place persuade him to hide outside Hermoupolis for the good of the church, and drowns him with a stone about his neck in the Nile — the same death saint.gr gives the Abibus of 13 Μαρτίου, which is the second Greek row below.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Αβίβος από την Ερμούπολη»

attestations.note: The second Greek day, kept as «Άγιος Αβίβος από την Ερμούπολη. Its page holds one sentence and a bracket: he was from Hermoupolis of Egypt and took the crown of martyrdom after a great stone was bound to his body and he was thrown into the river, «(Ίσως είναι το ίδιο πρόσωπο με τον Άγιο Σαβίνο τον Αιγύπτιο, βλ. 16 Μαρτίου )» — perhaps he is the same person as the holy Sabinus the Egyptian, kept on 16 March. **The author ruled on 3 October 2026 that he is** and this record is the merge of the two folders the corpus held. The hedge is one-sided: it is the 13 March page that raises it and the 16 March page says nothing back, which is why the life keeps the bracket in the source’s own words. The day gives no year and no hymn. The two differ in the name and in nothing else about the death: a stone bound to the body and the river.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 29.03.2026 (16. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Савин.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep in this folder, and the same man: an Egyptian of the city of Hermopolis and its chief man, hidden in a hut on a mountain, betrayed by a beggar he had fed, taken with six others and drowned in the Nile. The Prologue dates it 287, which falls inside the reign of Diocletian this folder already holds from doxologia; a sourced interval is not narrowed on a reading, so no date was touched. It prices the betrayal at two gold pieces, which neither other page does. The stored form is the bare forename: Свети мученик is the rank and the heading gives no city, so Hermopolis and the Egyptian by-name the Romanian and Greek forms carry are nowhere in it. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Sabin, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nestricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Sabin Egipteanul

english.text: Thy martyr Sabinus, O Lord, in his contest received the crown of incorruption from Thee, our God; for having Thy power, he cast down the tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At his prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Κηρύξας εὐσεβῶς, ἀσεβῶν ἐναντίων, τῶν πάντων Ποιητήν, σαρκωθέντα ἀτρέπτως, Σαβῖνε παμμακάριστε, ἱερῶς ἠνδραγάθησας· ὅθεν ἔφθασας, πρός ἀφθαρσίας χειμάῤῥουν, τέλος ἅγιον, ἐν ποταμῷ δεδεγμένος· διὸ εὐφημοῦμέν σε.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α’, Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτήρ, on the page of Άγιος Σαβίνος ο Αιγύπτιος. It names him and turns on the river. The page prints a kontakion in Ἦχος β´ and a kathisma in Ἦχος γ’ beside it.

english.text: Having preached in piety, against the impious, the Maker of all things made flesh without change, all-blessed Sabinus, you did valiantly in a holy way; and so you came to the torrent of incorruption, receiving a holy end in a river. Therefore we praise you.

hymns.text: Πρός ὕδωρ ζωῆς, καὶ πέλαγος χρηστότητος, ἰθύνθης σαφῶς, ἱστίῳ τῷ τοῦ Πνεύματος, ποταμίοις ὕδασι, προσριφείς Σαβῖνε πανεύφημε· διὸ λύσιν ἁμαρτιῶν, ὀμβρίζεις ἀπαύστως, προσευχαῖς σου ἡμῖν.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β´, Τά ἄνω ζητῶν, on the same page.

english.text: Cast into the waters of a river, you were steered plainly to the water of life and the sea of kindness by the sail of the Spirit, all-praised Sabinus; and so you rain down on us without ceasing the loosing of sins by your prayers.
